title: Merchandise Purchases — Refund Accounting Rules for Returns, Cancellations and Uncollected Pickups
content:
## Rules

**R1 Timing.** A received return of a Merchandise Purchases unit is refunded within the class's refund period in business days.

**R2 Amount.** The refund of a returned unit is its net paid amount — which already reflects price adjustments and excludes Finch Notes, which come back only as a reinstated note under the Finch Circle rules — less the restocking fee, the return fee and the gift-with-purchase deduction. It includes the unit's remaining sales tax as the tax refunded.

**R3 Restocking fee.** The restocking fee is the class's restocking percentage of the refunded merchandise (the net paid amount less the tax refunded), rounded half up to the cent. It is charged on all returns when the class charges it on all items, and on returns of opened, unused units when the class charges it on opened items.

**R4 Return fee.** The return fee is the class's prepaid label fee for a return by mail with a prepaid label, and its carrier pickup fee for a carrier pickup. In-store returns and returns mailed with the customer's own postage have no return fee.

**R5 Waivers.** No restocking fee and no return fee is charged when the return reason is one of the class's fee-waiver reasons. A Finch Circle member whose tier held on the return date waives the restocking fee pays no restocking fee, and one whose tier carries free return shipping pays no prepaid label fee; the carrier pickup fee still applies.

**R6 Gift with purchase.** For a class that deducts a kept gift with purchase, the class's gift-with-purchase value is deducted when a gift received with the unit is not returned with it.

**R7 Delivery fee.** The home delivery fee of the unit is not refunded unless the return reason is a fee-waiver reason; it is refunded only where the class makes it refundable on return or the return reason is a fee-waiver reason.

**R8 Destination.** With an original receipt or order record, the refund goes to the original tender — spread by the class's tender order for a mixed-tender unit, and mailed as a check when a cash refund is above the class's check threshold. A gift-receipt return goes to a merchandise credit card. A no-receipt return follows the rules for returns without a receipt. A registry gift returned by the registrant follows the rules for gift and registry returns.

**R9 Cancellations.** A cancellation or an uncollected pickup is refunded at the full net paid amount to the original tender, with no fee.

**R10 Once per return.** No refund has already been issued for the same return.

**R11 Other effects.** Sales tax is refunded per the class's sales tax refund basis. Finch Circle points and qualifying spend are reduced for the return where the class reduces them. Price adjustments, points and qualifying spend follow their own rules.

## Worked refund (hypothetical figures)

An opened, unused unit of a class that charges a 15 percent restocking fee on opened items, returned as changed mind by mail with a $9.95 prepaid label; net paid amount $214.00, of which $14.00 is remaining sales tax; the customer's Finch Circle tier waives nothing.

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Refunded merchandise: $214.00 less $14.00 | $200.00 |
| Restocking fee: 15 percent of $200.00, rounded half up | $30.00 |
| Return fee (prepaid label) | $9.95 |
| Refund: $214.00 less $30.00 less $9.95 | $174.05 |
| of which tax refunded | $14.00 |

Returned instead as defective — a fee-waiver reason — the same unit is refunded the full $214.00.

## Points of judgement

- A unit returned in store carries no return fee whatever its class.
- A Finch Circle member whose tier carries free return shipping and who returns a unit by carrier pickup still pays the carrier pickup fee.
- A second refund for a return that already shows a refund is not issued.
